reference.name: Higashiyama Onsen (Aizu Higashiyama Onsen, 東山温泉)

sources.quote: 東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。
is a hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Higashiyama Onsen with Aizu alias; Aizuwakamatsu, Fukushima, Japan all correct.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Aizu Higashiyama Onsen in Aizuwakamatsu, Fukushima — correct.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Same onsen district, correct admin fields.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
is a hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu

facts.rationale: Ja Wikipedia places it ~3 km southeast of Tsuruga Castle along the Yugawa (湯川); japan-guide confirms the valley setting.

sources.quote: Aizu is the westernmost of the three regions of Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.
Aizu Domain was a feudal domain under the Tokugawa shogunate which ruled most of the region from Aizuwakamatsu Castle.

facts.rationale: Aizu is the western region of Fukushima; the domain was ruled from Aizuwakamatsu Castle in the Edo period. Background fact about the region, not the onsen itself.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
Along the Yukawa River that runs through the town, classic Japanese inns remain to this day

facts.rationale: Inns line the 湯川 through a narrow valley; 'Yukawa' is a romanisation used by some sources (ja wiki reads it Yugawa).

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる
Higashiyama Onsen was opened by Reverend Gyoki 1300 years ago led by a 3-legged crow according to a legend.

facts.rationale: Supported by ja.wikipedia (opened in the 8th century, attributed to Gyoki, as tradition). Resolved numeric=true: the fact carries a date (8th century), consistent with Fa1106d81/Faa1b4ff4 which both labellers marked numeric.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
is a hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu

facts.rationale: Valley just east (strictly southeast) of central Aizuwakamatsu, on the 湯川 (Yu River = Yugawa).

sources.quote: Aizuwakamatsu is located in the western part of Fukushima Prefecture, in the southeast part of Aizu basin.
東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。

facts.rationale: Supported (japan-guide: valley 'just east of the downtown area'; ja.wikipedia: ~3 km SE of Tsuruga Castle). Resolved trivial=false: adds position in the hills east of the centre and 'northern Honshu', not only identity fields; consistent with Ff4a94e9b.

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる
Higashiyama Onsen was opened by Reverend Gyoki 1300 years ago led by a 3-legged crow according to a legend.

facts.rationale: Gyoki attribution and ~1,300-year history both stated by sources.

sources.quote: 東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。
is a hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu

facts.rationale: Restates identity: hot-spring area in Aizuwakamatsu.

Aizu domain association is supported, but no reliable source links novelist Higuchi Ichiyo to Higashiyama Onsen (sources name Yosano Akiko and Takehisa Yumeji instead); the Ichiyo claim is likely false but could not be refuted with a quote.

sources.quote: 江戸時代には会津藩の湯治場として栄え、会津若松の奥座敷として発展した。

facts.rationale: Ja Wikipedia: flourished as the Aizu domain's toji (bathing) place in the Edo period.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。

facts.rationale: Inns and hotels are concentrated along the Yugawa valley.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
are hot springs and the bathing facilities and traditional inns around them

facts.rationale: Hot-spring sources (1,500 L/min), 20+ inns; bathing facilities are part of any onsen area. 'Communal' facilities not separately documented.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。

facts.rationale: Valley resort just east of downtown Aizuwakamatsu; 'eastern edge' refers to the urban area (the municipality extends further east).

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。

facts.rationale: Hot-spring inns and hotels (20+) operate along the river.

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる

facts.rationale: Tradition: opened by Gyoki in the 8th century.

sources.quote: Higashiyama-ku, meaning "east mountain"
Aizu is the westernmost of the three regions of Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.

facts.rationale: 東山 literally 'east mountain'; Aizu is the region name.

sources.quote: 硫酸塩泉（カルシウム・ナトリウム-硫酸塩・塩化物温泉）
鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。

facts.rationale: Spring type is calcium-sodium sulfate-chloride; 20+ inns use it.

sources.quote: Aizuwakamatsu is located in the western part of Fukushima Prefecture, in the southeast part of Aizu basin.
東は磐梯山・猪苗代湖を含む奥羽山脈、南は会津高原と呼ばれる山間地、西は越後山脈、北は飯豊山地に囲まれている。

facts.rationale: Resort lies in the hills east of the city on the basin's eastern rim; the basin is ringed by mountains.

sources.quote: 硫酸塩泉（カルシウム・ナトリウム-硫酸塩・塩化物温泉）

facts.rationale: Resolved to B: sulfate type is confirmed (ja.wikipedia; official site 'sodium-sulphate hot springs'), but neither cited page nor a further search gives any reliable source calling the water 'gentle' or 'suited to long soaking' (official site only says 'Slowly unwind your mind and body'); half the claim is unsourced promotional bathing advice, so unverifiable.

sources.quote: Aizu is the westernmost of the three regions of Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.
東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。

facts.rationale: Supported (japan-guide: 'hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu'; en.wikipedia Aizu). Resolved trivial=false: beyond the identity fields it adds the relative position (eastern edge of the city), consistent with Ff4a94e9b which both labellers marked non-trivial.

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる
江戸時代には会津藩の湯治場として栄え、会津若松の奥座敷として発展した。

facts.rationale: Not founded by a Portuguese mission in 1742; tradition dates it to Gyoki in the 8th century (and Portuguese were barred from Japan after 1639).

sources.quote: are hot springs and the bathing facilities and traditional inns around them
In Japan, onsen are hot springs and the bathing facilities and traditional inns around them.

facts.rationale: Onsen means hot springs with the bathing facilities and inns around them.

sources.quote: 東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。
開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる

facts.rationale: Historic hot-spring area in Aizuwakamatsu; restates identity.

sources.quote: 江戸時代には会津藩の湯治場として栄え、会津若松の奥座敷として発展した。
During the Edo period, it was popular with the Aizu samurai, and developed as a retreat area.

facts.rationale: Toji (therapeutic bathing) place of the Aizu domain that developed in the Edo period.

sources.quote: 東山温泉（ひがしやまおんせん）とは、福島県会津若松市にある温泉。
is a hot spring resort in a valley just east of the downtown area of Aizu Wakamatsu

facts.rationale: Restates identity.

sources.quote: Memorials were erected for the poet Yosano Akiko and the painter of beautiful women, Takehisa Yumeji.
竹久夢二や与謝野晶子の歌碑があり、文人たちに愛されていたことがわかる。

facts.rationale: Takehisa Yumeji (and Yosano Akiko) are commemorated with memorials at the onsen; 'known in literature and art' is mild.

sources.quote: 江戸時代には会津藩の湯治場として栄え、会津若松の奥座敷として発展した。
会津藩指定保養所の歴史を持つ「向瀧」

facts.rationale: Edo-period toji place of the Aizu domain, popular with Aizu samurai.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
Along the Yukawa River that runs through the town, classic Japanese inns remain to this day

facts.rationale: Yugawa runs through the town with inns along it; valley sides are wooded.

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる
江戸時代には会津藩の湯治場として栄え、会津若松の奥座敷として発展した。

facts.rationale: Recognised as a historical onsen village in Aizu.

sources.quote: 鶴ヶ城から南東に約3km、湯川（ゆがわ）沿いに温泉宿・ホテル計20軒以上が営業している。
Along the Yukawa River that runs through the town, classic Japanese inns remain to this day

facts.rationale: Valley location on the river written Yukawa/Yugawa (湯川).

sources.quote: 開湯は8世紀後半、または天平年間に行基によってなされたと伝えられる
山形県の上山温泉、湯野浜温泉とともにかつて奥羽三楽郷と呼ばれた

facts.rationale: Tenpyo era is in the Nara period; counted among the three great old onsen of Tohoku (Ou Sanrakkyo).
